crit: 'three benchmark datasets of increasing complexity, MNIST, CIFAR-10 and ImageNet'; datasets and models 'of increasing complexity' so conclusions drawn 'on simple task' can be verified on 'how they scale to more complex ones'; ILSVRC-2012 'widely used as a benchmark'; imbalance is induced artificially (step and linear imbalance, 'representatives of most of the real-world cases').
notes: Multi-class image benchmarks (10, 10 and 1000 classes); nothing binarised. Step imbalance (rho, mu) and linear imbalance (rho) are induced on the training sets only; test sets stay balanced. Minority classes: random subset per repetition (MNIST), lowest label values (CIFAR-10), classes with <1000 cases plus randomized selection for the highest imbalance (ILSVRC-2012). 'Natural' not coded: the original (unmodified) datasets are only used to report the test error of the training setup (MNIST <1%, CIFAR-10 9.75%, ILSVRC-2012 top-1 62.56%), not in the imbalance experiments; adjudicator may consider it. No link to data or code. Supplementary Appendix A repeats CIFAR-10 step-imbalance experiments with reshuffled stratified train/test splits; Appendices B-C are plots/confusion matrices only.
